prompts.text:
Simon is a big liar. Simon's brother Jim knows this, he knows that Simon never tells the truth! Now yesterday Simon stole Jim's ping-pong paddle, and Jim knows Simon has hidden it somewhere, though he can't find it. He's very cross. So he finds Simon and he says, "Where is my ping-pong paddle? You must have hidden it either in the cupboard or under your bed, because I've looked everywhere else. Where is it, in the cupboard or under your bed"? Simon tells him the paddle is under his bed. 
Why will Jim look in the cupboard for the paddle?

During the war, the Red army captures a member of the Blue army. They want him to tell them where his army's tanks are; they know they are either by the sea or in the mountains. They know that the prisoner will not want to tell them, he will want to save his army, and so he will certainly lie to them. The prisoner is very brave and very clever, he will not let them find his tanks. The tanks are really in the mountains. Now when the other side asks him where his tanks are, he says, "They are in the mountains." 
Why did the prisoner say that?

Brian is always hungry. Today at school it is his favourite meal-sausages and beans. He is a very greedy boy, and he would like to have more sausages than anybody else, even though his mother will have made him a lovely meal when he gets home! But everyone is allowed two sausages and no more. When it is Brian's turn to be served, he says, "Oh, please can I have four sausages, because I won't be having any dinner when I get home!" 
Why does Brian say this?

Jill wanted to buy a kitten, so she went to see Mrs. Smith, who had lots of kittens she didn't want. Now Mrs. Smith loved the kittens, and she wouldn't do anything to harm them, though she couldn't keep them all herself. When Jill visited she wasn't sure she wanted one of Mrs. Smith's kittens, since they were all males and she had wanted a female. But Mrs. Smith said, "If no one buys the kittens I'll just have to drown them!" 
Why did Mrs. Smith say that?

One day Aunt Jane came to visit Peter. Now Peter loves his aunt very much, but today she is wearing a new hat; a new hat which Peter thinks is very ugly indeed. Peter thinks his aunt looks silly in it, and much nicer in her old hat. But when Aunt Jane asks Peter, "How do you like my new hat?," Peter says, "Oh, its very nice." 
Why does he say that?

Helen waited all year for Christmas, because she knew at Christmas she could ask her parents for a rabbit. Helen wanted a rabbit more than anything in the world. At last Christmas Day arrived, and Helen ran to unwrap the big box her parents had given her. She felt sure it would contain a little rabbit in a cage. But when she opened it, with all the family standing round, she found her present was just a boring old set of encyclopedias, which Helen did not want at all! Still, when Helen's parents asked her how she liked her Christmas present, she said, "It's lovely, thank you. It's just what I wanted." 
Why did she say this?

Late one night old Mrs. Peabody is walking home. She doesn't like walking home alone in the dark because she is always afraid that someone will attack her and rob her. She really is a very nervous person! Suddenly, out of the shadows comes a man. He wants to ask Mrs. Peabody what time it is, so he walks toward her. When Mrs. Peabody sees the man coming toward her, she starts to tremble and says, "Take my purse, just don't hurt me please!"
Why did she say that?

A burglar who has just robbed a shop is making his getaway. As he is running home, a policeman on his beat sees him drop his glove. He doesn't know the man is a burglar, he just wants to tell him he dropped his glove. But when the policeman shouts out to the burglar, "Hey, you! Stop!," the burglar turns round, sees the policeman and gives himself up. He puts his hands up and admits that he did the break-in at the local shop. 
Why did the burglar do that?

Brian is not doing well in school. He is worried about telling his parents that he is failing several of his classes and may have to retake the year. Today, the teacher informed the class that there will be a meeting with the parents on Monday. When Brian's mother comes to pick him up from school, his teacher says to her, "See you at the parent-teacher meeting! We have a lot to discuss." Brian's mother asks him when the meeting is, and he replies, "Tuesday."
Why did Brian say that?

Kate is employed in a company. She's been working there for few years now, but she is looking for a new job with a better salary. Today she had a job interview for a similar position in a different company. During the interview, the interviewer asked her how much she was earning in her current position. Kate replied with a figure that was 20% higher than her real salary
Why did Kate say that?

Mary's mother is very strict and always scolds her when she does something careless. Mary and her close friend Simon are eating ice cream together when Mary accidentally drops the ice cream on her backpack, which makes a big stain. When Mary's mother arrives, she asks Mary sternly what happened to her backpack. Simon says that he accidentally dropped his ice cream on Mary's backpack. 
Why did Simon say that?

Jack suspects that his wife Cheryl is cheating on him. The only hint he has is a mobile phone number he saw on Cheryl's mobile and which is not saved in her phone's address book. Today Jack came home from work earlier than usual and finds a plumber working at a broken sink. While Cheryl was talking to the plumber, Jack saw her laughing and smiling at him. Before the plumber left, Jack called the number he found on Cheryl's phone.
Why did Jack do that?

responses.response: Jim will look in the cupboard for the paddle because he wants to confirm whether Simon is lying or telling the truth. Despite knowing that Simon is a big liar, Jim wants to eliminate all possibilities and make sure he has thoroughly searched for the missing ping-pong paddle. By checking the cupboard, he can verify Simon's statement and rule out that particular location as the hiding spot for the paddle.

The prisoner said that because he knew that the Red army expects him to lie in order to protect his own army. By saying that the tanks are in the mountains, he deliberately provides false information, hoping to deceive the captors and mislead them away from the actual location of the tanks, which is by the sea. The prisoner's intention is to safeguard his army's position and prevent the Red army from discovering the true whereabouts of the tanks.
Brian says this in an attempt to convince the person serving the food to give him four sausages instead of the allowed two, by claiming that he won't be having any dinner when he gets home.

Mrs. Smith said that to stress the need for finding homes for the kittens. She wanted to make it clear that if nobody bought them, she would have to resort to drowning them. She was trying to highlight the urgency of the situation and convince Jill to consider adopting one of the kittens, so they wouldn't come to any harm.

Peter says that because he wants to be polite and avoid hurting Aunt Jane's feelings. He knows that Aunt Jane is proud of her new hat and may feel happy and confident wearing it. To show respect and maintain a harmonious relationship with his aunt, Peter chooses to compliment the hat by saying it's "very nice," even though he personally dislikes it.

Helen said this because she wanted to demonstrate her appreciation for her parents' gift and to avoid hurting their feelings. Despite feeling deeply disappointed that her long-awaited rabbit was not the present she received, she made a conscious decision to respond positively and express gratitude. Helen understood the effort her parents had put into selecting the gift and wanted to show them that she valued their gesture and recognized their intentions. By saying the gift was "lovely" and "just what I wanted," Helen aimed to maintain a harmonious and appreciative atmosphere during the Christmas celebration.

She said that because Mrs. Peabody, being a very nervous person, assumed that the man approaching her in the dark intended to harm her. Her fear of being attacked and robbed overwhelmed her, leading her to make a desperate plea for him to take her purse instead of causing her harm. Mrs. Peabody's immediate reaction was driven by her anxious nature and a desire to protect herself from potential harm in a situation that triggered her fears.

The burglar did that because he mistook the policeman's shout as a sign that he had been caught or recognised for robbing the shop. Thinking that the policeman was onto him, the burglar quickly surrendered by putting his hands up and confessing to the break-in at the local shop to avoid the hassle.

Brian said that because he wanted to put off his parents' realisation of his academic difficulties. By stating that the parent-teacher meeting is on Tuesday instead of Monday, he hoped to buy himself some extra time. Brian was trying to delay the meeting in the hopes that he could improve his grades or find a solution before his parents found out that he is failing his classes.

Kate said that her current salary was 20% higher than her actual earnings because she wanted to negotiate for a higher salary in her potential new job. By inflating her current salary, Kate hoped to create the perception that she already earns a higher amount, thereby increasing her chances of securing a better salary offer from the new company. This tactic is commonly used during salary negotiations to leverage one's perceived value and increase the likelihood of receiving a more favorable compensation package.

Simon said that he accidentally dropped his ice cream on Mary's backpack to protect Mary from getting scolded by her strict mother. Knowing that Mary's mother would be angry and reprimand Mary for being careless, Simon took the blame for the accident in order to spare Mary from facing the consequences. By accepting responsibility and shifting the focus away from Mary's mistake, Simon showed his loyalty and willingness to protect his friend from getting into trouble.

Jack dialed the number he found on Cheryl's phone because he had a feeling that something fishy was going on. Suspecting that Cheryl might be cheating on him, he wanted to dig deeper and gather more information. By making the call, he hoped to find out who was on the other end of the line and get some clues or evidence regarding Cheryl's possible affair. Jack's decision to call the number shows that he wanted to confront his suspicions head-on and uncover the truth about his wife's behavior.

Short answer: Because Simon is a liar - or at least that is what we know from what is written about him above. So, it is likely his brother Jim won't believe Simon's response to his query regarding where he (Simon) has hidden the paddle, and Jim will therefore look in the place where Simon inferred he did not hide the paddle.
 
 Long answer: Jim believes his brother Simon has stolen his ping-pong paddle and has hidden it either under his (Simon's) bed or in the cupboard. Jim demands to know where Simon has hidden the paddle. But Jim is very precise in the way he words his demand to his brother and provides Simon with only one of two possible answers to choose from - either 'under the bed' or 'in the cupboard'. Perhaps Jim was using a kind of process-of-elimination strategy on Simon - by keeping his question quite precise and limited (in terms of possible hiding places) - because Jim is well aware that his brother is a big liar. Simon tells Jim he hid the paddle under the bed, but because Simon tells lies, Jim is likely to suspect his brother's response will be a lie also. Therefore, Jim will look in the cupboard first. :)

I can only guess why she would say such a thing. 
 She could have been making a sarcastic, dark joke; we don't know if Jill and Mrs Smith know each other well, or anything about their history. We do know that Jill knows a woman nearby has kittens she want to give away, so they could be close neighbours or even friends.
 Or perhaps Mrs Smith is trying to make Jill feel guilty, manipulating her into getting one of the male kittens. If they don't know each other well, Jill might feel pressured to take one.

I think Peter didn't want to make his aunt feel bad about her hat. He may also think that, being an older woman who's into hats, and him a younger man, he may be in no position to comment on her hat. In that case, there's no real harm in telling this lie. The aunt will feel happy with his response.

I imagine she didn't want to make her parents sad. However, we don't know how she said what she said. It migh've been clear from her delivery that even though she said she liked it, she in face didn't like it and the parrents may have picked on that. Or she could have said in in a believable way making the family think she liked the gift.
 
 Depending on how she said it, it could show she really wanted to let the family know she didn't like it without saying it explicitly, OR she really didn't want them to know she was disappointed. The reason she didn't want them to know could be not wanting to hurt their feelings or she might be worried about their reaction.

I think that considering what we know about her, the reaction was understandable; all the things she fears seem to be about to happen. In her mind, the man was waiting in the shadows and her worries and expectations led her to react that way. There was no way for her to know if there was any ill intent from the man so she thinks offering her purse will result in her not being harmed.

We don't know anything about how experienced this burglar is, his age, build, etc. This leads me to think he was scared of any physical confrontaton. He may also have felt that the officer knew he was a burglar and that ultimately there was no way to escape. What the officer said sounds quite aggressive; if the officer was just trying to catch the burglar's attention, he could've shouted "excuse me" or something less aggressive. Perhaps the burglar thought that it would be better to admit everything and he might be punished less harshly.

I think Brian is hoping that if his mother misses the Monday meeting, she won't find out he's not doing well in school. If he's quite young, he might believe this, but I can't imagine and older child believing this. If he's older, he might have just panicked without thinking through the longer consequences of his school and mother communicating with each other in the future.

Kate wants a higher salary; if she says her current salary is higher than it is, then she's hoping the new company will offer at least that or probably more (in the event of a job offer). 20% may have been a figure she thought was actually what she shoud be getting based on the her prior research of the position, therefore it was reasonable to not be truthful. She may have heard that this is a good tactic to use, but of course, depending on the country she's in, this interview question may or may not be something the new employer could check. If not, there's no harm in telling a lie, but if they can check, then it could look bad for her (meaning she's taking a risk).

I think Mary must've told her friend about her mother's personality. Simon was concerned Mary would be punished and he wanted to protect her. He's counting on the fact that parents probably don't want to scold or punish other people's children.

I think Jack wanted to see if the plumber's phone would ring. This would either put his mind at ease knowing that she'd called in a plumber without needing to save the number for the future, or leave him continuing to wonder who's number it really is. Since he already suspects an affair, if the number turns out to be the plumber's he may also think that his wife is interested in the plumber.

Jim will look in the cupboard for the paddle because, as stated at the beginning of the story, Simon is a big liar who never tells the truth. So when Simon says the paddle is under his bed, Jim assumes he is lying, and thus he thinks the paddle must be in the cupboard.

The prisoner said that the tanks are in the mountains, which is actually the truth, because he knows that his captors, the Red army, believe that he will lie to protect his army. Given this belief, if he tells them the tanks are in the mountains, they will assume that he's lying and thus will search for the tanks by the sea, thereby preserving the real location of his army's tanks in the mountains. His clever strategy is to tell the truth, counting on his captors' expectation of a lie to mislead them.

Brian says this because he wants more sausages than he is allowed. He knows the standard serving is two sausages, but he's trying to convince the server to give him extra by making them believe he won't have any dinner at home. Even though this is not true, as his mother will have prepared a meal for him, Brian is using this excuse to try and get more sausages because he is very greedy.

Mrs. Smith said that she would have to drown the kittens if no one buys them as a way to persuade Jill (and potentially other buyers) to take the kittens, despite any initial reservations they might have. Given that Mrs. Smith loves the kittens and wouldn't want to harm them, her statement is likely not a genuine intention but rather a tactic to create a sense of urgency or induce guilt, aiming to encourage adoption.

Peter says that the hat is very nice because he cares about his Aunt Jane's feelings and doesn't want to hurt them. Even though he personally finds the hat to be ugly, he decides to say something positive about it to make his aunt happy. This is a common social situation where people often prioritize the feelings and emotions of others over expressing their own honest opinion, particularly when the truth might cause distress or upset.

Helen said this because she didn't want to disappoint her parents or appear ungrateful for the gift they had given her. Even though she was truly disappointed that she didn't receive the rabbit she had wanted, she chose to hide her feelings to maintain a happy and positive atmosphere on Christmas Day. Her response is an example of a common social behavior, where people sometimes hide their true feelings to avoid causing distress or discomfort to others, especially in group or family settings like this one.

Mrs. Peabody said that because she is a very nervous person who fears being attacked and robbed when walking home alone in the dark. Seeing a man coming towards her out of the shadows triggers her fear, leading her to assume that he intends to rob her. Even though the man merely wants to ask the time, Mrs. Peabody preemptively offers him her purse in an attempt to avoid any potential harm, misinterpreting his intention based on her fears.

The burglar did that because he misinterpreted the policeman's intention. He assumed the policeman was shouting at him because he knew about the burglary, causing him to panic and confess. The burglar, being in a state of heightened alertness due to his recent illegal activity, misconstrued the policeman's call about the dropped glove as an indication that he was caught for the robbery. This is a case of misunderstanding caused by his guilty conscience and fear of being apprehended for his crime.

Brian said the parent-teacher meeting was on Tuesday because he is trying to delay the inevitable conversation about his poor academic performance. He knows that his parents will find out about his failing grades during this meeting, so by misinforming his mother about the correct day of the meeting, he hopes to postpone their discovery and the subsequent discussion, perhaps out of fear, embarrassment, or a desire to avoid disappointing his parents.

Kate said that because she is aiming to get a higher salary in her new job. If she disclosed her real current salary, the new company might offer her only a slight increase. By inflating her current salary by 20%, she is hoping that the new company will offer her a significantly higher pay rate based on the inflated figure. This is a common strategy used by job seekers during salary negotiations, although it can be risky if the potential employer verifies the salary information with the current employer.

Simon said that he accidentally dropped his ice cream on Mary's backpack to protect Mary from her mother's scolding. He knows that Mary's mother is strict and would likely reprimand Mary for being careless. By taking the blame, Simon is attempting to shield Mary from her mother's criticism, showing his loyalty and care for his friend. This action suggests Simon is willing to face potential consequences himself in order to spare Mary.

Jack called the number he found on Cheryl's phone because he was suspicious of his wife's behavior and wanted to verify if his suspicions were correct. Seeing Cheryl laugh and smile with the plumber might have fueled his suspicions further. By calling the unknown number while the plumber was still present, Jack might have hoped to observe if the plumber's phone rang, indicating that the number belonged to him and potentially confirming his suspicions about Cheryl's infidelity.
